title: edge-networking-deltas-and-workarounds-oct-2026
body:
Weekly field notes + standup digest (hand-off for on-site engineers)

Context:
- Customer: Oakmont Health (pilot VPC + on-prem KV/cache pair)
- Current phase: network hardening + telemetry enablement after initial install (post-ship week 2)
- Goal: unblock canary traffic and complete production handoff

Attendees (10/12 sync): Priya Kumar, Liam Chen, Maya Patel, Diego Alvarez, Customer NOC (S. Haines)

Top symptoms observed this week:
1) Intermittent token-serving stalls (p95 latency spikes) when model shards cross private-link boundary. Correlated with bursts from customer query generator.
2) Packet drops and TLS handshake failures on intra-datacenter 10G link during peak (customer reports 1-2% packet loss only when flow size > MTU).
3) Missing exporter data in Redwood Console for two on-prem nodes (node-exporter metrics stop for 12–20 minutes then recover).

Root-cause signals / hypotheses:
- MTU mismatch between customer ToR switch (configured at 9000) and BGP peers on our edge (default 1500) causing fragmentation and reassembly pressure in the NIC stack.
- Customer firewall boxes are performing deep packet inspection that occasionally terminates TLS re-handshake when TCP MSS > path MTU — observed on packet captures.
- iptables rules deployed by customer team accidentally dropped ephemeral port ranges used by our sidecar exporter health checks (iptables DROP rules added in their hardening script).

Workarounds applied (field):
- Temporary TCP MSS clamp applied at the host (1500 -> 1452) for affected interfaces. Patch script: ops-config/patches/mss-clamp-1452.sh (PR linked above).
- Canary routing: moved Redis/KV traffic to a static route via dedicated backbone interface that bypasses the customer's DPI appliance for now. This reduced p95 stalls by ~40% in the canary.
- Exporter sidecar: launched a UDP-based heartbeat probe from the edge router to on-prem nodes so Console shows node "up" even if exporter data drops briefly. Known limitation: this does not replace full Prom metrics.

Customer blockers still outstanding:
- Customer is uncomfortable with permanent MSS clamp; wants DPI vendor on-site to confirm fix. Estimated ETA: vendor window 10/20.
- Two firewall rules still in their hardening profile that drop ephemeral ports 32768–60999; customer security wants a formal exception request.
- On-prem rack power sequencing behavior inconsistent after a brownout (BIOS of one host flips to BMC-only mode). Need replacement spare or BIOS patch.

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego: Create a minimal runbook for MSS clamp rollback and safe validation steps (due 2026-10-14).
- Liam: Open vendor engagement ticket with DPI vendor, capture vendor contact + support window (Jira INF-4123 comment) (due 2026-10-13).
- Maya: Draft customer exception request template for ephemeral port range and route maps; sync with security (due 2026-10-15).
- Priya: Schedule on-site escalation call with customer NOC + DPI vendor for 10/20, confirm remote access window (due 2026-10-16).
- Field engineer checklist: verify node-exporter permissions, iptables ACCEPT for 9100 + ephemeral ranges, confirm ntp drift < 2s (owner: field team, due 2026-10-13).

Temporary mitigations we recommend for other installs:
- Add MTU validation step to preflight: probe end-to-end MTU (IPv4/IPv6) and fail fast in preflight if mismatch > 200 bytes.
- Add optional TCP MSS clamp toggle in onboarding script with automated rollback if loss decreases below baseline.
- Add a lightweight UDP heartbeat exporter as a fallback when Prom ingest dips; include it as an opt-in flag in private installer.

Telemetry gaps discovered:
- Missing TCP retransmit counters in our default dashboard for on-prem installs — dashboard relies on node-exporter netstat that the customer's hardened image strips.
- No fallback flow logs captured from the ToR (customer does not forward sFlow). We should add a guide for enabling basic flow sampling at 1:1000 during install.

Risks / notes to leadership:
- If vendor engagement slips beyond 10/27, we risk delaying production handoff by two weeks due to customer compliance requirements.
- Current workaround (static route) reduces redundancy; if primary link fails we will need fallback plan (recommend temporary dedicated VPN tunnel to secondary region).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Can we get a signed temporary exception from customer security to allow ephemeral range during hardening window? (Pending).
- Should we permanently add MSS clamping to our supported private profiles or treat as emergency-only? Need product guidance.

Meeting minutes (10/14 ad-hoc):
- Customer NOC confirmed brownout logs; BIOS vendor identified (SuperMicro). Field engineer recommended a non-invasive firmware pin to avoid BMC-only boot state — awaiting vendor approval.
- DPI vendor initial triage: packet captures show TLS re-handshake drop correlated with large initial window; vendor suspects middlebox bug when TLS session resumption occurs across NAT; vendor requested additional full pcap during repro window.

Next steps / sprint tie-ins:
- INF-4123: vendor engagement and capture of vendor RCA (owner: Liam).
- OPS-233: add MTU probe to installer preflight + ms-s clamp toggle (owner: infra eng).
- DOCS-91: new private-install checklist additions + telemetry fallback guidance (owner: docs).

Notes-to-self / quick reminders:
- Keep the static-route as a last-resort flag in ops-config; tag it with "manual-fallback" to avoid accidental promotion to infra-as-code.
- Capture full pcap early in the repro window; set tcpdump rotation to small files to avoid disk pressure.

Appendix (field commands used):
- sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1452
- sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 0.5% delay 5ms (used briefly for repro)
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/onprem_repro.pcap -s 0 'tcp port 443' (rotate every 50MB)

If you pick this up as the on-call or field lead: read INF-4123 first, then run the preflight MTU probe and confirm the ephemeral port exception request draft in DOCS-91 before talking to the customer.

— Priya K.
